newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Kazakh cbanker sees $300 mln borrowing this year.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh cbanker sees $300 mln borrowing this year.

text.p: Kazakhstan plans to borrow up to $300 million this year, probably in Eurobonds of not less than five years maturity, National Bank chairman Uraz Dzhandosov said on Friday.
"In the second half or in the autumn, we plan to borrow in the range of $300 million, most probably Eurobonds," Dzhandosov told reporters at the Central and East European Economic Summit.
He said the Kazakh authorities were currently in talks to select lead managers for the issue. Asked when they would be appointed, he said, "I think within 10 days from now."
The Central Asian state issued a debut $200 million, three-year Eurobond last December, priced to yield 9.3 percent or 350 basis points above comparable U.S. Treasury notes.
Moody's Investors Service last year assigned Kazakhstan a Ba3 sovereign rating for long-term foreign currency bonds. Standard & Poor's rated the former Soviet republic BB-.
